name: z80asm
desc: Assembler for the Zilog Z80 microprcessor and compatibles
why: A Z80 assembler opens the door to retro 8-bit programming and the machine code that drove a generation of home computers.

brief.what_it_is: z80asm is a free assembler for the Zilog Z80 microprocessor and compatible chips. You feed it Z80 assembly source files and it produces a binary output file. It can also write a label file listing every label in the program, and a listing file that puts the source and the assembled bytes side by side. Source files can include other source files and contain conditional sections. The homepage says it is written in ANSI C and has been tested on GNU/Linux.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a goal of having a free, easy to expand, easy to use assembler, with the GPL license so users can read, modify and redistribute the source. The Savannah page adds that it aims to be portable and complete, and that it was written with the MSX computer in mind as the target, though it works for any system with a Z80.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes the inputs and outputs but not the internals. Source files are assembled with bash-style expressions and can include other files and use conditional blocks. The label file can be included by other source files, which gives linker-like behaviour across separately assembled pieces. Some header files with MSX BIOS, BDOS and system-variable labels are bundled.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond a C compiler and the usual source build was mentioned. The homepage says it is ANSI C and should compile on any good platform, but it has only been tested on GNU/Linux. I did not see build steps, a configure line, or a binary download on either page. The brew formula name is z80asm and the executable is z80asm.
brief.standout: The label file can be included by other source files, so separately assembled pieces can link together without a separate linker. It also ships MSX-specific header files of BIOS, BDOS and system-variable labels, which is unusual for a general-purpose assembler.
brief.status: Quiet, not clearly maintained. The Savannah summary lists Development Status as 4 - Beta, registration in November 2003, 20 open bugs out of 31 total, and 1 open patch out of 12. Four members are listed, with Bas Wijnen as group admin. I could not find a last release date or last commit date on either page.
brief.caveats: Only tested on GNU/Linux according to the homepage. Development status is Beta. The homepage's link to the documentation says only "here" and I could not find its URL, so I did not read the full manual. The Savannah page says the project is not part of the GNU Project itself even though it is hosted on Savannah and the homepage is under nongnu.org. The README does not give a version number or changelog.
quotes: The goal of The Z80 assembler project is having a free, easy to expand, easy to use assembler. Free as in free speech, that is.
Very complex expressions are allowed (bash style).
Beside the binary output file, a label file can be output with a list of all labels in the program.
